bull.b: Okta’s sustained ~77% gross margin and a return to operating profit provide durable economics typical of a scalable SaaS platform. Strong gross margins support reinvestment in product, fund go-to-market expansion, and improve free cash flow generation, underpinning multi‑period profitability resilience.

bull.t: Strong balance sheet and capital flexibility
bull.b: About $2.6B of cash and low leverage give Okta flexibility to navigate investments, settle liabilities, or return capital. This liquidity buffer supports execution on product rollouts and M&A, smooths near‑term settlements, and lowers refinancing risk, strengthening medium‑term financial resilience.

Net retention ~107% and an increasing large‑customer mix (about 85% of ACV) signal durable enterprise adoption and expansion potential. Higher ACV, upsell from new products, and larger land deals translate into more predictable recurring revenue and stronger long‑term customer lifetime value.

bear.t: AI products remain early-stage and not yet material
bear.b: While AI agent bookings drive larger deals and pipeline, the business acknowledged these offerings are early and not yet meaningful to revenue. That delays scalable monetization, so anticipated AI-driven growth and margin benefits could take multiple quarters to materialize, increasing execution risk.

bear.t: Rising AI inference costs and pricing uncertainty
bear.b: Escalating inference/tooling costs and unclear agent pricing models create structural margin pressure as AI usage scales. If Okta must absorb higher costs or cannot reliably monetize agent usage, margin sustainability and free cash flow conversion could be impaired over the medium term.

bear.t: Near‑term cash outflow from convertible note settlement
bear.b: A ~$350M cash settlement of maturing convertible notes is a concrete near‑term capital drain. Even with strong cash, this reduces available liquidity for buybacks, reinvestment, or acquisitions and temporarily compresses free cash flow metrics, creating execution sensitivity across the next several quarters.
